newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on Sammi trouble pressure.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on Sammi trouble pressure.

text.p: Seoul stocks ended Thursday slightly lower after its earlier plunge was nearly erased by hopes for a raise in the foreign stock ownership ceiling, brokers said.
But Sammi Group's financial difficulties remained a dark cloud over the bourse, leading 79 stocks to end limit low.

In the late afternoon, investors renewed hopes the finance and economy ministry would announce the limit expansion. But after the market closed, Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik said: "I have not considered the matter at all." The stock index ended 3.43 points lower at 642.86, off a day low of 630.37.
Brokers, watching the televised news conference, said the announcement was disappointing.

"Today's announcement had no real details and was more like a rallying call for everyone to try harder," market analyst Kim Myung-ho of Hyundai Securities. "This isn't going to turn the market around, and investors -- especially individuals -- were disappointed."
Brokers said with no announcement of a ceiling expansion, the market would plunge tomorrow.
"It will not take a long time for the index to breach the 600 line," said broker Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities.

But Yoon Jeung-hyun, deputy minister for the financial policy division, said: "What Minister Kang really means is he was not informed about the matter...It's our official stance that we are still considering the limit earlier than planned."
Brokers said the market was still focused on the Sammi Group failure as it triggered jitters among investors about a possibile financial crisis.

"You can imagine what will happen in small companies with financial problems in the wake of Sammi's failure, which is one of the nation's top 30 groups," said analyst Park Key-pyong of Hanyang Securities.
Sammi Steel defaulted on 1.8 billion won debt obligations and creditor banks froze its checking accounts.
"The underlying market sentiment is really fragile as many investors are worried about the possibility of a financial crisis due to the failure of Hanbo Steel and Sammi Steel," Hanyang's Park said.
Concerns about tightening liquidity was reflected in the money market. Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds continued to trade at a 18-month high of 12.85 on Thursday. The won hit 884.90.
The Sammi woes continue to deal a heavy blow to financial shares. Its sub-index plummetted 3.56 percent to 452.11.
"Banks made so many bad loans and securities houses acted as gaurantors," Hyundai's Kim Myung-ho said.

Korea First Bank lost 70 won to 2,900 after hitting a 1997 low of 2,810. Commercial Bank of Korea went limit down of 320 won to 3,730. The two banks are major lenders of Sammi Steel and Sammi Corp respectively.
